title: Scalar finite-projective dual realization on a ringed site
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings equipped with a morphism $\underline R\to B$, where underlines denote constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category $D(B)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $C_B(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ for ordinary $R$-modules, using ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective $R$-modules, with degreewise finite-free retract data [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], and put $E^\bullet=C_B(F^\bullet)$ termwise. Define $F^{\vee,\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(F^\bullet,R[0])$ with
$$(F^{\vee,\bullet})^q=\operatorname{Hom}_R(F^{-q},R),\qquad d^q(\phi)=-(-1)^q\phi\,d_F^{-q-1}$$
[def-pur-hom-complex]. Each $E^q$ is a direct summand of a finite free $B$-module sheaf, and $\mathcal Hom_B(E^q,-)$ is exact. For every K-injective resolution $B[0]\to I^\bullet$, the comparison
$$\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0])\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$$
is a quasi-isomorphism, so its source represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every finite projective $R$-module $V$, the canonical sheaf morphism
$$\beta_V:C_B(\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R))\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B),\qquad \beta_V(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\phi(v)$$
is an isomorphism natural in $V$. Applied to $V=F^{-q}$, these maps form an isomorphism of cochain complexes
$$C_B(F^{\vee,\bullet})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0]),$$
with the displayed signed differentials, hence give a natural isomorphism $C_B(F^{\vee,\bullet})\simeq R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B)$ in $D(B)$. If $F^\bullet$ is zero outside $[a,b]$, both dual complexes are zero outside $[-b,-a]$. No flatness of $B$ over $\underline R$ is assumed.

proof.text: For any finite projective scalar module $V$, finite generators give a surjection $p:R^N\to V$, and the projective lifting property lifts $1_V$ to $i:V\to R^N$, with $pi=1_V$. Put $v_j=p(e_j)$ and $\lambda_j=e_j^*i\in V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$. Then $v=\sum_j\lambda_j(v)v_j$ and, by applying $\phi\in V^*$, $\phi=\sum_j\phi(v_j)\lambda_j$. For the terms of $F^\bullet$ use the supplied splittings. These identities also cover $V=0$ with $N=0$.

source.place: Tags 05CE/05CF, definition-projective and lemma-characterize-projective, lifting the identity through a finite free surjection

proof.text: Constant sheafification takes the supplied scalar splitting to the constant splitting, with $\underline{R^N}\cong\underline R^N$, exactly as specified in the coefficient-package definition. The sheaf tensor definition gives the coordinate isomorphism $C_B(R^N)\cong B^N$: $b\otimes(r_j)_j\mapsto(br_j)_j$, with inverse $(b_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$. These maps are balanced and commute with restriction, so extend to sheafifications. Additivity and functoriality give $C_B(p)C_B(i)=1$ and $C_B(0)=0$. Thus $C_B(V)$ is a retract of $B^N$, and in particular each $E^q$ has the required finite-free retract. No tensor-exactness assertion is used.

proof.text: Apply the finite-retract internal-dual lemma with coefficient sheaf $B$, $T=E^q$, and the splitting just constructed. Its exactness clause states that $\mathcal Hom_B(E^q,-)$ carries every short exact sequence of module sheaves to a short exact sequence. This is exactness of internal sheaf Hom, not exactness of global Hom or of sections.

For a scalar $V$, the evaluation formula $\beta_V(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\phi(v)$ is additive and balanced in both tensor expressions, is $B$-linear, and commutes with restriction. Finite-product preservation of sheafification extends the bilinear evaluation, so the tensor universal property gives a map into the sheaf Hom. Explicitly, first define evaluation on constant local sections and extend along the two sheafifications; the formula is unchanged after restriction. For $f:V\to W$, the two composites from $C_B(W^*)$ to $\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B)$ both send $b\otimes\psi$ and $b'\otimes v$ to $bb'\psi(f(v))$. The uniqueness part of sheafification extends this equality to all sections. Thus $\beta$ is contravariantly natural in $V$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final evaluation map; explicit scalar/sheafification formula

proof.text:
Use the dual generators from step 1. On every localized site, for $h:C_B(V)|_U\to B|_U$, set $\gamma_V(h)=\sum_j h(1\otimes v_j)\otimes\lambda_j\in C_B(V^*)(U)$. The finite sum commutes with restriction, hence defines a sheaf morphism. On tensor generators,
$$\beta_V\gamma_V(h)(b'\otimes v)=b'\sum_jh(1\otimes v_j)\lambda_j(v)=h(b'\otimes v),$$
while
$$\gamma_V\beta_V(b\otimes\phi)=\sum_jb\phi(v_j)\otimes\lambda_j=b\otimes\phi.$$
The dual-generator identities and sheafification uniqueness make these identities hold on all sections. Therefore $\gamma_V$ is the inverse of $\beta_V$. The comparison is independent of the chosen splitting because its defining evaluation formula is; its inverse is then uniquely determined.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite-free/direct-summand calculation; explicit inverse to scalar evaluation

proof.text:
In degree $q$, the only possibly nonzero factor of $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0])$ is $\mathcal Hom_B(E^{-q},B)$, and the Hom-complex differential is $h\mapsto-(-1)^q h\,d_E^{-q-1}$. Use $\beta_{F^{-q}}$ for its degree-$q$ comparison. Naturality from step 4 applied to $d_F^{-q-1}:F^{-q-1}\to F^{-q}$ gives, on generators,
$$d_{\mathcal Hom}\beta(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=-(-1)^qbb'\phi(d_F^{-q-1}v)=\beta C_B(d_{F^\vee})(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v).$$
Hence the degreewise isomorphisms form the claimed cochain isomorphism. They are natural in cochain maps by the same precomposition identity. If $F^r=0$ outside $[a,b]$, $F^{-q}=0$ outside $[-b,-a]$; $C_B(0)=0$ and the displayed unique-factor formula give the stated vanishing for both dual complexes, including the zero complex.

proof.text: The complex $E^\bullet$ is bounded since its zero terms remain zero, and each term has exact internal Hom by step 3. Apply the bounded-exact-term Hom lemma to $P=E^\bullet$ and the quasi-isomorphism $B[0]\to I^\bullet$ of any K-injective resolution. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary unbounded source and target complexes of this map, so it gives precisely the asserted quasi-isomorphism of Hom complexes for every such resolution. By the definition of derived internal Hom the target represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B)$, with the canonical identification for any K-injective resolution. Composing its inverse in $D(B)$ with the cochain isomorphism of step 6 gives the required derived isomorphism. Taking the fixed functorial resolution makes the comparison natural; the definition's canonical independence of resolution identifies the other choices with it. All constructions used only finite splittings and internal-Hom exactness, so no flatness of $B$ over $\underline R$ was used.
